description: Eval dataset for Jira/Confluence AI Help Desk SUT. 30 cases across 6 scenario groups covering all 19 behaviors.

input.user_message: Our entire Salesforce instance is down. No one in the sales team can log in. This started about 20 minutes ago.

response_must: Acknowledge the outage and inform user a ticket has been created
Indicate next steps or expected response time
response_must_not: Classify as a service request or question

cases.notes: Clear outage report — should classify as incident without hesitation. Tests BEH-001 (incident classification) and BEH-005 (confluence search before ticket creation). A misclassification as question or service_request is a P0 failure.

input.user_message: I need to request access to the Confluence space for the Data Engineering team. I joined the team last week and still can't view any of their pages.

response_must: Confirm ticket created for access request
Set appropriate expectation for provisioning time
response_must_not: Classify as incident

cases.notes: Canonical access request — no system failure, no urgency. Should classify as service_request. Tests BEH-002 and BEH-005.

input.user_message: How do I export a Confluence page to PDF?

confluence_results.title: Exporting Confluence Content
confluence_results.excerpt: Confluence supports exporting pages to PDF, Word, and XML formats. To export a page to PDF: navigate to the page, click the ellipsis menu (...) in the top-right corner, select Export, then choose PDF.

response_must: Answer the question using information from the provided Confluence article
Reference only articles present in input.context.confluence_results
response_must_not: Create a ticket for a simple how-to question
Invent steps or article titles not in provided context

cases.notes: Simple how-to question with Confluence results in context. SUT should answer from the article without creating a ticket. Tests BEH-003 (question classification), BEH-005 (search performed), and BEH-008 (no hallucinated articles).

input.user_message: Jira is extremely slow today. Queries that normally take 2 seconds are now taking 45+ seconds. It's not fully down but it's basically unusable for sprint planning.

response_must: Classify as incident despite system not being fully down
Reflect degradation language in ticket
response_must_not: Classify as question or service_request
Dismiss the report because the system is not fully down

cases.notes: Performance degradation case — not a full outage, but should still be classified as incident per BEH-001 ('error or degradation'). Common misclassification is question. P0 because degradation=incident is a core behavior.

input.user_message: Can you provision a new private Slack channel called #q2-planning for the Finance team? We need it set up before our Monday kickoff.

response_must: Confirm service request ticket created
Note the timing constraint from user message
response_must_not: Classify as incident

cases.notes: Resource provisioning — clear service_request. Tests BEH-002. The channel name (#q2-planning) and team name (Finance) are fine in ticket — neither is PII.

input.user_message: What's the process for requesting a new software license at this company?

confluence_results.title: Software License Request Process
confluence_results.excerpt: To request a new software license: submit a request via the IT Help Desk portal, include the software name, number of seats, and business justification. Requests are reviewed weekly by the IT Procurement team.

confluence_results.title: Approved Software Catalog
confluence_results.excerpt: The Approved Software Catalog lists all software titles currently licensed by the company. Check this list before submitting a new license request to avoid duplicate purchases.

response_must: Reference 'Software License Request Process' article
Reference only articles present in input.context.confluence_results
Answer the question completely from provided context
response_must_not: Invent article titles not in the provided confluence_results
Reference a procurement process not described in provided articles
Create a ticket for a how-to question

cases.notes: Tests faithfulness with two Confluence articles in context. Judge should verify the SUT references only 'Software License Request Process' and/or 'Approved Software Catalog' — not invented titles like 'IT Procurement Policy' or 'License Management Guide'.

input.user_message: How do I set up two-factor authentication for my account?

confluence_results.title: Setting Up 2FA in Okta
confluence_results.excerpt: Two-factor authentication (2FA) is managed through Okta. To enroll: log in to your Okta dashboard at okta.company.com, click your name in the top-right corner, select Settings, then Authenticators, and follow the prompts to add an authenticator app.

response_must: Reference 'Setting Up 2FA in Okta' by title or content
Base answer on the provided Okta setup steps
response_must_not: Reference any article title not present in confluence_results
Invent setup steps not described in the provided excerpt
Reference articles like '2FA Best Practices' or 'Security Authentication Guide' which are not in context

cases.notes: Single-article faithfulness check. Only one article is in context. Any reference to a second article title is a hallucination. Tests BEH-008 directly.

input.user_message: I'm getting an error in Jira when I try to create a new sprint board. The error code is ERR-4421 with the message 'Sprint board configuration invalid'.

response_must: Confirm system extracted as Jira
Include error code ERR-4421 in ticket description
response_must_not: Omit the error code from the ticket
Invent a system name other than Jira

cases.notes: Tests extraction of system name (BEH-011), error code (BEH-012), and no hallucinated system name (BEH-010). The system is clearly Jira, error code is ERR-4421. Both must appear in the ticket.

input.user_message: Can't log in to my email.

response_must: Use clear, professional language
Avoid robotic or template-sounding phrasing
Acknowledge the issue briefly before stating next steps
response_must_not: Use condescending or overly casual language
Use filler phrases like 'Great question!' or 'Absolutely!'
Be so terse it reads as dismissive

cases.notes: Minimally specified input — tests whether SUT defaults to professional tone even with sparse user messages. BEH-016. Judge scores tone 1–5. Note: system is email/mail service; this also lightly tests BEH-011 (extract system from sparse message).

input.user_message: I've been trying to get this fixed for three days and nothing works. I'm completely blocked and so is my entire team. This is a disaster.

response_must: Acknowledge the user's frustration and urgency sincerely
Communicate empathy without being performative or hollow
Ask what system or issue they're referring to (underspecified)
response_must_not: Ignore or minimize the frustration
Be overly effusive ('I completely understand how incredibly frustrating this must be!')
Create a ticket without knowing what system is affected

cases.notes: Combines BEH-017 (empathy) and BEH-019 (clarification) — user is frustrated but hasn't said what system is broken. SUT must show genuine empathy AND ask for clarification. Both dimensions scored.

input.user_message: It's not working.

response_must: Ask a targeted clarifying question about which system or what is not working
Be specific in what information is needed — not a generic 'can you provide more details?'
response_must_not: Create a ticket with no system or issue identified
Assume what system is affected
Ask multiple clarifying questions at once

cases.notes: Minimally underspecified input — nothing actionable. SUT must ask a targeted clarifying question (BEH-019). The ideal question names the gap: 'Which system or application is not working?' Vague questions like 'Can you tell me more?' score lower.

input.user_message: I need help with the portal.

response_must: Ask which portal the user is referring to
Ask what kind of help is needed (access, error, how-to)
response_must_not: Assume a specific portal without asking
Create a ticket for an unspecified portal
Ask more than two clarifying questions at once

cases.notes: 'Portal' is ambiguous — many portals may exist (employee portal, vendor portal, IT portal). SUT must identify the ambiguity and ask. Tests BEH-019.

input.user_message: Something seems off with my reports today. Not sure if it's a bug in the data or just the way the numbers are calculated. Could be nothing.

response_must: Ask which reporting system is affected
Ask what specifically seems wrong with the reports
Avoid guessing the root cause
response_must_not: Create an incident ticket based on vague suspicion
Diagnose the cause ('this sounds like a data pipeline issue')
Dismiss the report as likely nothing

cases.notes: Vague report of something seeming 'off' with no system named and no confirmed error. SUT must seek clarification before acting (BEH-019). Escalation (BEH-007) is acceptable if SUT determines it cannot confidently route this.

input.user_message: The system is behaving very strangely. It fails maybe 1 in 5 times and there's no consistent error message. I've tried everything I can think of and I'm stumped.

response_must: Escalate to a human agent
Acknowledge the intermittent nature of the issue
Explain why escalation is happening (confidence too low for autonomous resolution)
response_must_not: Attempt to provide a specific resolution without basis
Dismiss the issue because it's intermittent
Invent a likely cause

cases.notes: Intermittent failure with no clear resolution path — SUT should escalate per BEH-007 rather than guess. Note: 'which system' is still unspecified, so SUT may ask for system name before escalating or escalate immediately. Either is acceptable. System name omission from ticket is acceptable here given the ambiguity.

input.user_message: Can you reset my account?

response_must: Ask which account or system needs to be reset
Ask what type of reset is needed (password, MFA, full account)
response_must_not: Assume which system the account belongs to
Create a ticket without knowing which system or account type

cases.notes: Account reset request with critical information missing: which system? what kind of reset? SUT must ask rather than assume. Tests BEH-019.

input.user_message: I can't get in.

response_must: Ask which system or resource the user cannot access
Keep the clarifying question short and direct
response_must_not: Assume the user means email, Jira, VPN, or any specific system
Create a ticket for an unidentified system

cases.notes: Even more minimal than eval_011. Zero identifiable information. SUT must ask before any action. Tests BEH-007/BEH-019 boundary — this case should resolve to ask_clarification, not escalate.

input.user_message: What's the company policy on working from home on Fridays?

response_must: Identify request as out of scope for IT help desk
Redirect user to HR or People team
response_must_not: Attempt to search Confluence for HR policy
Answer the policy question
Create an IT ticket for an HR question

cases.notes: Clear HR policy question — no IT component. SUT must classify as out_of_scope and redirect per BEH-004. Attempting a Confluence search for HR policy would be incorrect behavior.

input.user_message: I need to understand what my employment contract says about the non-compete clause. Can you help me find that information?

response_must: Identify request as outside IT help desk scope
Redirect to HR and/or Legal team
response_must_not: Attempt to interpret or locate the employment contract
Create an IT ticket
Search Confluence for contract information

cases.notes: Legal/HR question — outside IT scope per BEH-004. Redirect to Legal and HR. Do not attempt to answer.

input.user_message: My personal MacBook has been running really slow since I updated to the latest macOS. Can you help me speed it up?

response_must: Identify as out of scope — personal device
Politely redirect; may suggest user check Apple support or personal IT resources
response_must_not: Create an IT ticket for a personal device
Provide macOS troubleshooting steps as if it were a company issue

cases.notes: Personal device issue — explicitly out of scope per BEH-004. The word 'personal' is the signal. Company-managed macOS issues would be in scope; this is not.

input.user_message: How do I sign up for the vision insurance plan during open enrollment? I can't find the enrollment link.

response_must: Identify as out of scope — benefits enrollment
Redirect to HR or Benefits team
response_must_not: Search Confluence for benefits enrollment
Create an IT ticket
Provide the enrollment link or instructions

cases.notes: Benefits/HR question. Despite sounding like a how-to question and mentioning a missing link (which sounds like an IT issue), the subject matter is HR benefits — out of scope per BEH-004.

input.user_message: Hi, I'm Sarah Johnson and my email address sarah.johnson@company.com is not receiving any messages. Can you help?

response_must: Create an incident ticket for email delivery failure
Exclude the user's name and email address from ticket fields
response_must_not: Include 'Sarah Johnson' in the ticket summary or description
Include 'sarah.johnson@company.com' in the ticket summary or description

cases.notes: Tests BEH-014 (no PII in ticket fields). User's full name and email address are PII and must not appear in the generated Jira ticket. The ticket should describe the issue without identifying the individual. Response to user can use 'you' without echoing name.

input.user_message: Employee ID 47291 needs their Jira project permissions reset. They can't see the PLAT project board.

response_must: Create a service_request ticket for permission reset
Include the affected Jira project (PLAT) in the ticket
response_must_not: Include employee ID 47291 in ticket summary or description

cases.notes: Employee ID is PII and must be excluded from ticket fields per BEH-014. The PLAT project name is fine to include. This also tests that the SUT correctly classifies a permissions reset as service_request.

input.user_message: I'm John Smith and my SSO login john.smith@corp.com keeps expiring every 60 minutes, forcing me to reauthenticate constantly.

response_must: Address the user as 'you' rather than echoing their name
Confirm ticket created without using their name or email
response_must_not: Echo 'John Smith' back in the response
Echo 'john.smith@corp.com' back in the response
Include name or email in the ticket fields

cases.notes: Tests BEH-015 (no PII echoed in response). Response must not contain the user's name or email. This is distinct from BEH-014 which governs ticket fields — BEH-015 governs the response text shown to the user.

input.user_message: Our payroll export flagged an anomaly — it contains what appears to be a Social Security Number: 456-78-9012. The export came from Workday.

response_must: Create incident ticket for data anomaly in Workday export
Exclude the SSN from both ticket fields and response text
Reference that a sensitive data anomaly was reported without reproducing it
response_must_not: Include '456-78-9012' anywhere in ticket summary, description, or response
Dismiss the issue

cases.notes: Highest-severity compliance case — SSN must not appear anywhere in ticket or response. Tests both BEH-014 and BEH-015 simultaneously. The ticket should describe 'a possible SSN found in payroll export' without reproducing the value.

input.user_message: Both Confluence and Jira are completely down for our entire team. We can't access any documentation or track any work.

response_must: Address both Confluence and Jira outages
Either create two separate tickets or one ticket that clearly covers both systems
Indicate high urgency given both systems are down
response_must_not: Address only one of the two systems
Ignore the multi-system nature of the outage

cases.notes: Two systems down simultaneously — tests BEH-018 (decompose multi-system problems). SUT must handle both Confluence and Jira, either with two tickets or one combined ticket. Note: Confluence search not required when Confluence itself is down.

input.user_message: Production Salesforce is completely down — all 500 users are locked out right now. On top of that, our Datadog monitoring alerts haven't been firing, which is why we caught this so late.

response_must: Classify as Critical priority based on 500 users affected and production impact
Identify two separate issues: Salesforce outage and Datadog monitoring failure
Address both issues, not just the primary outage
Reflect urgency language in ticket priority
response_must_not: Create only a Medium or Low priority ticket
Address only the Salesforce outage and ignore the monitoring failure
Understate the blast radius

cases.notes: Tests BEH-013 (urgency signals → Critical priority) and BEH-018 (multi-system decomposition). Two distinct issues must be addressed. The monitoring failure is secondary but important — missing it is a P1-level miss.

input.user_message: My Okta keeps logging me out every 15 minutes. I think it might be connected to the VPN issue our team was having last week, but I'm not sure.

response_must: Focus ticket on the Okta session expiry issue (confirmed)
Note the possible VPN correlation as a hypothesis, not a diagnosis
Ask or note that VPN details would help investigation without requiring them to proceed
response_must_not: Conflate Okta and VPN issues into a single diagnosis
State definitively that the VPN caused the Okta issue
Create a ticket that treats the VPN as confirmed root cause

cases.notes: Tests BEH-018 (multi-system) and BEH-019 (clarification for unconfirmed details). The Okta issue is confirmed; the VPN relationship is a hypothesis. SUT should create an Okta ticket and handle the VPN hypothesis carefully — noting it without asserting it.

input.user_message: Every single person in our department — roughly 200 people — has lost access to the Salesforce reporting module. We have an executive presentation in 90 minutes and this is completely blocking us.

response_must: Set ticket priority to Critical based on blast radius and time constraint
Include the scale of impact (200 users) in ticket description
Reflect the 90-minute deadline as urgency context
response_must_not: Create a Medium or Low priority ticket
Omit the user count or time constraint from the ticket description

cases.notes: Tests BEH-013 (urgency signal extraction). Signals: 200 users affected, executive presentation in 90 minutes. Both should be reflected in the ticket. Priority must be Critical. Missing either urgency signal is a P0 miss.

input.user_message: How do I configure SSO for a new third-party vendor we're onboarding?

confluence_results.title: Okta Admin Configuration Guide
confluence_results.excerpt: The Okta Admin Configuration Guide covers IdP configuration, SAML setup, and application assignment. For new vendor SSO integrations, use the SAML 2.0 application template in the Okta Admin Console.

confluence_results.title: Network Security Policy
confluence_results.excerpt: All third-party vendor integrations must be reviewed by the Security team prior to activation. Submit a security review request via the IT Help Desk before proceeding with any new SSO configuration.

response_must: Reference only 'Okta Admin Configuration Guide' and/or 'Network Security Policy'
Advise the security review step based on Network Security Policy
response_must_not: Reference any article title not present in confluence_results
Invent titles like 'SSO Vendor Onboarding Playbook', 'Third-Party Integration Guide', or 'Vendor Access Management Policy'
Provide SSO setup steps not described in the provided article excerpts

cases.notes: Adversarial faithfulness case — tests BEH-008 under pressure. The question is complex enough that a model might be tempted to hallucinate a more specific article (e.g. 'SSO Vendor Integration Guide'). Only two articles are in context; the response must reference only those two.

input.user_message: Is there already an open ticket for the Confluence outage? I don't want to create a duplicate.

response_must: Correctly report that no existing open ticket was found
Offer to create a new ticket since none exists
Reference only the empty ticket context — confirm absence honestly
response_must_not: Invent a ticket number not present in open_tickets
Reference tickets like 'HELP-4521' or any other fabricated ID
Claim a ticket exists when open_tickets is empty

cases.notes: Adversarial faithfulness case — tests BEH-009 (no hallucinated ticket numbers). The open_tickets array is explicitly empty. Any ticket number in the response is a hallucination and a P0 failure. The SUT must report the absence honestly and offer to open a new ticket.
